clue.text: Ill-fated, floored by mishap

indicators.note: 'by' means beside, so one piece is placed directly after the other

parts.note: a mishap is an accident
someone floored is lying flat on the ground

explanation.surface: Someone knocked to the ground by a misfortune is described as ill-fated.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps having mishaps seems dogged by bad luck, so the compound adjective serves as a loose synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps real celeb has brains

indicators.note: 'perhaps' suggests one possible version of the letters, so they may be rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a genuine celebrity might actually be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is the rear part of the brain; the plural is used loosely here for brains in general.

clue.text: Mad when son leaves, being silly

indicators.note: the son leaving means the letter standing for son is taken out of the word for mad

parts.note: mad means insane
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent goes mad and acts foolishly once their son moves out.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes something empty-headed and pointless, a straightforward synonym of silly.

clue.text: Name the pet I treated

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A vet's instruction to record the name of the animal just treated.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or title given to someone, so it is a kind of name.

clue.text: Drama taking place in surgery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the stage and plays generally
second meaning: the room in a hospital where operations are performed

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene unfolds during an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama taking place' reads as one phrase; split it after 'Drama' and the rest is a hospital room.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is both the art of plays and, in British usage, short for operating theatre in a hospital.

clue.text: Resume meeting about veneer outside study

indicators.note: 'outside' says the rearranged letters wrap around the word for study
'about' suggests turning things around, so the letters of the surface word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to con is to study or pore over a text

explanation.surface: A committee picks up its discussion of wood veneer after a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Con, meaning to study, is old-fashioned but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to gather again after an adjournment, which is to resume a meeting.

clue.text: Most of revenue returned in no time!

definitions.note: the answer means at no time

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards
'most of' means the word loses its final letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that most of the tax take came back almost instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last two letters of the word for income, then read the rest backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Never is the adverb meaning at no time whatever.

clue.text: Drug used against his volunteers and mine

parts.note: anti means against
taken as written
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug to counter both his volunteers and their own.
explanation.walkthrough: TA stands for the Territorial Army, the British army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihistamine is a medicine taken against allergies, so it is an example of a drug.

clue.text: Faulty method: circular delivered upside down

parts.note: faulty means wrong
a method is a way of doing something
circular means round

explanation.surface: A leaflet posted the wrong way up is an inefficient method of delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a leaflet pushed through doors; here it is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upside down is inverted, positioned the opposite of how it should be, a near-synonym phrase.

clue.text: A bishop interrupted native's story

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written, the outer word
taken as written
Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric breaks into a local person's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: RR is short for Right Reverend, the formal style of an Anglican bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, a synonym for a story.

clue.text: Hide some recent discoveries

indicators.note: 'some' says only a part of the following words is wanted

parts.note: the letters sit wholly inside the second word, from its third letter to its seventh

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceal certain new findings.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover something is to conceal it from view, a straight synonym of hide as a verb.

clue.text: Steep, if main base's under escarpment originally

indicators.note: 'originally' points to the origin, the start, of each word

parts.note: the initial letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A military or geological note about a base sited below a steep slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for a slope; here it is the verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to saturate it, and imbue likewise means to soak or permeate thoroughly.

clue.text: Cricketers hope to do it, though it's a kind of accident

definitions.meaning: first meaning: batters strike the ball and set off for a run
second meaning: a collision where the driver flees the scene

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, batters score by hitting the ball and running between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both a batting action in cricket and a road collision in which the driver fails to stop.

clue.text: The Italian legal term was prohibited

parts.note: il is the Italian for the
licit is a formal word for lawful

explanation.surface: A legal expression from Italy was banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means not permitted by law or custom, so it is a synonym of prohibited.

clue.text: Stick with new colour; you'll firstly gain clarity

parts.note: to cohere is to stick together
N is the abbreviation for new
C is an abbreviation for colour

indicators.note: 'firstly' says only the opening letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Advice that sticking with a fresh colour scheme will make things clearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherency is the quality of being logical and easy to follow, which is clarity of thought or expression.

clue.text: Facial hair's classy, said the Cockney

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the initial H, so the word is heard as that Londoner pronounces it

parts.note: classy is highbrow; without its H it sounds like the facial feature

explanation.surface: A Cockney compliments someone's stylish facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, are famous for dropping the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyebrow is the strip of hair above the eye, one kind of facial hair.

clue.text: Scoop mere fabrication: write it again!

indicators.note: a fabrication is something made up or constructed, so these letters are built into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An editor tells a reporter that a made-up scoop must be rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: To recompose is to compose anew, that is to rewrite a piece of writing or music.

clue.text: Diner serving drinks on the hop

indicators.note: 'on' means placed next to, so one piece is attached to the other

parts.note: teas are drinks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A busy diner serves drinks while rushing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the hop' looks like a single phrase meaning busy, but it splits into a positional word and a word taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A teashop is a small café serving light meals, so it counts as a kind of diner.

clue.text: Legendary piper ace with a universal remedy

parts.note: Pan, the Greek god who played pipes
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mythical piper, brilliant at his craft, holds a cure for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure for all ills, literally a universal remedy.

clue.text: Incomplete drawing put in front of you initially

indicators.note: placing one thing ahead of another means the pieces join in that order

parts.note: a sketch is a rough drawing

indicators.note: 'initially' points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: An unfinished drawing is placed before you.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy describes something lacking detail or not thorough, which is a sense of incomplete.

clue.text: Set about ward manager

indicators.note: 'about' suggests moving things around, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital ward's manager is told to set to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward manages an estate, household or event, so the word is a synonym for a manager.

clue.text: Indian aristocrat to hear a mean criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An Indian noblewoman sits in judgement over a cruel offender.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharanee is the wife of a maharaja or a ruling princess in India, so an Indian aristocrat.

clue.text: Article in hall refers to food for Muslims

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such food

indicators.note: 'in' says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: taken as written, the outer word
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A notice in a dining hall describes the food served to Muslim diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal describes food prepared according to Islamic law, as eaten by observant Muslims.

clue.text: Speechless love for Disney character

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone is left speechless by their love for a cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is the flying elephant from the 1941 Disney film, an example of a Disney character.

clue.text: In depression, so became an alcoholic

parts.note: a dip is a hollow or depression in the ground
taken as written

explanation.surface: A depressed person turns to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but here it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipso is informal shorthand for dipsomaniac, a person with a craving for alcohol.

clue.text: Fabric found in any London market

indicators.note: 'found in' says the letters are sitting inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second
surface padding completing the picture of a stall

explanation.surface: A material on sale at any market stall in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'market' only completes the picture of a stall selling cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic material woven into cloth, an example of a fabric.

clue.text: Sudden repression of vice out of order

parts.note: a vice is a clamp for holding work
a machine that is out of order is said to be down

explanation.surface: Authorities suddenly crack down on wrongdoing that has got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' reads as wickedness but is the workshop tool; 'out of order' is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a sudden firm action by authorities to suppress something, a kind of repression.

clue.text: Show coy reluctance in drama that's difficult to acquire

parts.note: a play is a drama
something difficult to acquire is hard to get

explanation.surface: An actor shows bashful hesitation in a play whose tickets are scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: To play hard to get is to feign disinterest, especially in romance, a coy show of reluctance.
